claims.claim: Old Mr. Dashwood's Norland estate passes to nephew Henry, then at Henry's death to Henry's son John
claims.evidence: 'he left it to him on such terms as destroyed half the value ... to his son, and his son's son, a child of four years old'
claims.fix: estate left to Henry but tied up for John and John's small son

claims.claim: Henry's widow and three daughters are poorly provided for
claims.evidence: ten thousand pounds ... was all that remained for his widow and daughters

claims.claim: Henry Dashwood dies within a year of his uncle
claims.evidence: He survived his uncle no longer [than] one twelvemonth

claims.claim: John is Henry's son by a former marriage
claims.evidence: By a former marriage, Mr. Henry Dashwood had one son

claims.claim: Fanny pushes out stepmother and half-sisters
claims.evidence: 'Mrs. John Dashwood ... arrived with her child'; 'ungracious behaviour' to Mrs. Dashwood; Mrs. D. then leaves of her own accord
claims.fix: Fanny takes over Norland and makes them unwelcome

claims.claim: Mrs. Dashwood, Elinor, Marianne and Margaret move to Barton Cottage in Devonshire
claims.evidence: removing into Devonshire; 'Barton Cottage, though small, was comfortable'

claims.claim: Elinor loves Edward Ferrars
claims.evidence: Elinor's attachment throughout; 'marriage of Edward and Elinor'

claims.claim: Edward is secretly engaged to Lucy Steele
claims.evidence: 'four years' engagement'

claims.claim: Willoughby charms Marianne
claims.evidence: Willoughby and Marianne at Barton cottage

claims.claim: Willoughby abandons her to marry a rich heiress, Miss Grey
claims.evidence: 'Miss Grey has fifty thousand pounds'; 'every thing was then just settled between Miss Grey and me'

claims.claim: Marianne falls gravely ill
claims.evidence: 'delirium on Marianne's side' at Cleveland

claims.claim: Colonel Brandon nurses her back
claims.evidence: Elinor 'scarcely stirring from her sister's bed'; Mrs. Jennings 'attentive care'; Brandon only fetches their mother

claims.claim: Marianne learns restraint
claims.evidence: 'to counteract, by her conduct, her most favourite maxims'

claims.claim: Lucy marries Robert Ferrars
claims.evidence: 'my brother is lately married to ... Miss Lucy Steele'

claims.claim: Lucy's marriage frees Edward; Edward marries Elinor
claims.evidence: 'Edward was free'; 'marriage of Edward and Elinor'

claims.claim: Marianne marries Colonel Brandon
claims.evidence: 'a wife, the mistress of a family' ... 'Colonel Brandon was now as happy'

claims.claim: Elinor eldest sister, sensible; Marianne passionate, romantic
claims.evidence: chapter characterisation

claims.claim: Willoughby dashing young man who jilts Marianne
claims.evidence: as above

claims.claim: Colonel Brandon older, steady friend who loves Marianne
claims.evidence: 'Colonel Brandon loves Marianne. He has told me so himself.'; 'too old to be married'

claims.claim: Mrs. Jennings warm, gossiping friend
claims.evidence: 'talked a great deal ... full of jokes and laughter'
